Fix `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 review fix (person's decision). In actionChangeArrowheadSize's perform, the Medium branch (`value === DEFAULT_ARROWHEAD_SIZE`) currently does `element = newElementWith(el, {}, el.arrowheadSize !== undefined); delete (element as Mutable<ExcalidrawLinearElement>).arrowheadSize;`. When el has no changes newElementWith can return the scene's own object, so the delete mutates a scene element in place, and the `!== undefined` test misses an own key holding `undefined` (delta.ts leaves `arrowheadSize: undefined` after an undo), which then gets no version bump. Replace the Medium branch with: if `!("arrowheadSize" in el)` return `el` unchanged (no new object); otherwise build a fresh object without the key and never delete from the scene's object, e.g. `const { arrowheadSize: _arrowheadSize, ...rest } = el; element = newElementWith(rest as typeof el, {}, true);` so version/versionNonce are bumped and the result has no own "arrowheadSize" key. Keep the non-default branch (`newElementWith(el, { arrowheadSize: value })`) and the elbow re-route (`isElbowArrow(element) ? newElementWith(element, updateElbowArrowRoute(...)) : element`) as they are. Remove the `Mutable` import if it becomes unused. eslint must pass with --max-warnings=0 (if the unused destructured name is flagged, name it so the project's no-unused-vars config ignores it, e.g. a leading underscore, or use an equivalent omit).

Fix `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionStyles.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 review fix (person's decision). In actionPasteStyles, the arrow branch computes `shouldClearArrowheadSize = elementStylesToCopyFrom.arrowheadSize === undefined && newElement.arrowheadSize !== undefined`, calls newElementWith(newElement, {...}, shouldClearArrowheadSize) and then `delete (newElement as Mutable<typeof newElement>).arrowheadSize`, which can delete from a scene object and misses a target holding an own `arrowheadSize: undefined` key (left by delta.ts after an undo). Change it to test own keys with `in`: when the source has an own "arrowheadSize" key (`"arrowheadSize" in elementStylesToCopyFrom` and its value is not undefined), copy it as today. When the source has no own key (or holds undefined) and the target has an own "arrowheadSize" key (`"arrowheadSize" in newElement`), build the pasted element from a fresh object without the key, e.g. `const { arrowheadSize: _arrowheadSize, ...rest } = newElement; newElement = newElementWith(rest as typeof newElement, { startArrowhead: ..., endArrowhead: ... }, true);` (version bump, no delete on any scene object). Otherwise keep today's newElementWith call. Keep the following isElbowArrow re-route as is. Remove the `Mutable` import if it becomes unused. eslint must pass with --max-warnings=0.

instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/arrowheadSize.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 review: add assertions for the fixed Medium/paste behaviour (actionChangeArrowheadSize in packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx and actionPasteStyles in packages/excalidraw/actions/actionStyles.ts now never delete from a scene object, and turn an element holding an own `arrowheadSize` key, including one holding `undefined`, into a new element with no key and a bumped version). (a) In 'undoes and redoes arrowheadSize changes through history deltas' (or a new test after it): after undoing back to default (the element then holds `arrowheadSize: undefined` as an own key), keep `const before = h.elements[0]`, select it, click `screen.getByTestId("arrowheadSize-medium")`, then expect `"arrowheadSize" in h.elements[0]` to be false, `h.elements[0]` not to be `before` (`expect(h.elements[0]).not.toBe(before)`), and `h.elements[0].version` to be greater than `before.version`. (b) In the copy/paste test (or a new test): build a target arrow that holds an own `arrowheadSize: undefined` key, e.g. `{ ...API.createElement({ type: "arrow", ... }), arrowheadSize: undefined }`, put it in the scene with the default-sized source arrow (API.setElements), copy styles from the default-sized source, select the target, keep `before`, paste styles, then expect `"arrowheadSize" in` the pasted target to be false, it not to be `before`, and its version to be greater than `before.version`. Keep every existing test and assertion. Note API.createElement does not forward arrowheadSize (set it on the returned object) and API.setSelectedElements needs `as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement` casts. vitest and eslint --max-warnings=0 must pass.
